source.title: What Does Alignment Cost? The Structural Brittleness of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
source.authors: Joanna Hao; Shanduojiao Jiang; Sailaja Nakka

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies reasoning circuits in Llama-3.2 models on mathematical tasks. It cites the GPT-2 IOI circuit as background but does not test that circuit or its claims.
record.gate_note: The reported circuit-size and patching results concern mathematical CoT in Llama-3.2-1B and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, not GPT-2 IOI or the named IOI head classes. They are recorded as findings about a related but different behavior; they do not test any claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Wang et al. (2023) only as background on circuit discovery. Its experiments find attention-head circuits for mathematical CoT tasks in Llama-3.2-1B base and instruct models. It does not study IOI, GPT-2 small, or the IOI head classes. Its self-repair (Hydra effect) claim concerns math-reasoning circuits, not IOI name-mover backup heads, so it does not bear on V2 either.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that the base Llama-3.2-1B has redundant, self-repairing reasoning circuits (Hydra effect). The instruct model shows reduced redundancy, with more than double the necessity drop on synthetic primitives (6.79% vs 2.92%); they call this an 'Alignment Tax on Redundancy'. They note the absolute brittleness is modest at 1B, and that the two models converge on the GSM8K proxy.
record.recipe_differences: Not an IOI circuit replication. The study discovers attention-head circuits for mathematical CoT with single-head activation patching and applies dual-direction resample ablation to Llama models.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the larger circuit-size difference appears on abstract synthetic tasks, while the GSM8K-Proxy head counts and necessity drops are similar across the two models. They also state that discovery depends on the particular 8-shot prompt template.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3.2-1B, circuits found by single-head patching at an 80% cumulative-impact threshold are near-sufficient under denoising (about 99–101% recovery). Resample-noising them costs little: average necessity drop 2.92% for Base versus 6.79% for Instruct on synthetic tasks, and about 5% for both on the GSM8K proxy. The authors attribute the small drops to backup-head self-repair (Hydra effect) that is weaker after instruction tuning. Circuit sizes also differ: Instruct uses 95 heads versus Base's 57 on average across synthetic tasks, and 181 versus 68 on Parity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-repair or redundancy in attention-head circuits for algorithmic reasoning is reduced by instruction tuning in small Llama models.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 4th Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Foundation Models (KnowFM 2026)
record.problems: The evidence does not address the GPT-2 IOI claim. For its own study, the authors note the 1B-only comparison, synthetically generated tasks and GSM8K proxy, dependence on the 8-shot prompt template, attention-head-only intervention granularity, and inability to isolate alignment-training stages. No uncertainty estimates are reported in the presented results.

untested.parts: All: the GPT-2 small IOI circuit, its 26 heads in 7 classes, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
All: backup name-mover heads in IOI. Self-repair is inferred only for Llama math-reasoning circuits.
All: no IOI circuit or IOI head classes are examined in Llama or any other model.
All: no attempt to recover the IOI circuit with other methods, ablations or metrics.
All: no evaluation of the IOI circuit's sensitivity to ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
All: no IOI prompt variants are tested.

record.verdict_notes: Row links are correct: every row is ['none'] with state cannot_determine for IOI versions. Rows r1–r6 are circuit-size values produced by the discovery threshold (selection outputs), which is acceptable as descriptive context. The Hydra-effect attribution is an interpretation: no backup heads are identified directly. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 small IOI circuit, its 26 heads and 7 classes, and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Whether backup heads take over the role of ablated IOI name-mover heads.
Whether the IOI head classes and roles recur in other models or checkpoints, or are reused across tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover the IOI circuit.
Sensitivity of the GPT-2 IOI circuit evaluation to ablation, metric, or prompt distribution.
Whether the IOI circuit operates across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.
